new_symbol_range_suggestions.leak_conductance: positive; typically much smaller than 1/resistance, but large enough that leak_conductance*resistance is not negligible in observable leakage experiments
new_symbol_range_suggestions.leakage_voltage_scale: positive and within the same order of magnitude as observed capacitor voltages when thresholded leakage activation is to be visible

derivation_notes: The child adds a finite leakage branch across the capacitor that discharges stored charge through dielectric imperfections. To satisfy the required saturating_or_thresholded embedding, the leakage current is weak near zero capacitor voltage and transitions toward a voltage-proportional branch as Abs(V_C) exceeds leakage_voltage_scale, recovering ordinary parallel leakage at larger voltages.
change_summary: A leakage discharge term was added to the capacitor-voltage ODE, opposing charging with a response that activates over a finite voltage scale. This changes both the late-time curvature and the asymptotic capacitor voltage, unlike the parent's single ideal charging branch.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: The capacitor is not perfectly insulating; it has a finite parallel leakage path whose discharge effect becomes appreciable once a finite capacitor voltage is established.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: When leak_conductance -> 0, or when Abs(V_C) << leakage_voltage_scale so tanh(Abs(V_C)/leakage_voltage_scale) is negligible over the observation window, the added leakage term vanishes and the parent law is recovered.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: Relative to the ideal RC parent, trajectories with appreciable capacitor voltage show reduced late-time slope and saturation below source_voltage, with leakage influence small at very early times and stronger after V_C grows.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed resistance and capacitance, dV_C_dt depends only linearly on the voltage gap source_voltage - V_C, so all charging traces are single-exponential with one shared time constant.
response_change.child_relation: Add capacitor leakage as an extra discharge path proportional to V_C, so dV_C_dt depends on both the charging gap and the present capacitor voltage through a second linear channel; the effective approach rate and final saturation both change.
response_change.observable_effect: Compared across experiments with different source_voltage but the same component values, the leaked capacitor saturates below source_voltage and shows a different late-time curvature than the ideal single-exponential parent.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the capacitor has a finite leakage path on time scales comparable to the charging experiment, i.e. the leakage time constant is not much longer than resistance*capacitance and measurements extend into mid-to-late charging.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, leakage appears as slightly reduced late-time slope and sub-source saturation; in holdout with broader observation windows or larger source_voltage, the same mechanism more clearly reveals the lowered asymptote and altered curvature.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing leakage conductance, equivalently infinite leakage resistance.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A real capacitor can have a finite parallel leakage path through dielectric imperfections, producing a discharge current proportional to its own voltage during charging.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added term introduces a new voltage-dependent activation scale, so the target mapping is no longer a single globally linear function of source_voltage - V_C. This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because leakage influence is state-conditioned, changing curvature across the trajectory rather than merely rescaling one time constant.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: There is no leakage path across the capacitor.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The capacitor has a finite leakage path whose discharge contribution activates over a finite voltage scale and then approaches a voltage-proportional regime.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: (source_voltage - V_C) / (resistance * capacitance) - leak_conductance * V_C * tanh(Abs(V_C) / leakage_voltage_scale) / capacitance
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: leak_conductance -> 0, or operation restricted to Abs(V_C) << leakage_voltage_scale so the added term is negligible.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Charging remains monotone, but once V_C grows enough to activate the leakage branch, the curve bends away from the parent single-exponential approach and settles below source_voltage.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the early-time ideal charging slope and the reduced steady-state fraction across observation windows when leakage is appreciable. In the parent, resistance and capacitance jointly fix one time constant while the asymptote is locked to source_voltage; retuning those coefficients can slow or speed the whole trace but cannot lower the final voltage below source_voltage without spoiling the shared early-time relation.

evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing leakage conductance, equivalently infinite leakage resistance.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model omits capacitor leakage, treating the capacitor as perfectly insulating so no stored charge can drain except through the intended charging branch.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: There is no leakage path across the capacitor.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A real capacitor can have a finite parallel leakage path through dielectric imperfections, producing a discharge current proportional to its own voltage during charging.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to add leakage across the capacitor. The parent target mapping is a fixed-environment single-time-constant law: for fixed resistance and capacitance, changing source_voltage only rescales the same exponential approach, and the final voltage always equals source_voltage. Under the child mechanism, holding resistance and capacitance fixed while varying source_voltage still gives monotone charging, but the target slope depends on both source_voltage - V_C and V_C because leakage opposes charge accumulation. The concrete contrast is that late in the trajectory the parent predicts approach to source_voltage with a single shared asymptote ratio V_C/source_voltage -> 1, whereas the child predicts approach to a lower steady value set by the balance of resistor current and leakage current. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both the early-time charging rate and the reduced steady-state fraction across observation windows when leakage is appreciable, because the parent ties transient rate and asymptote through one ideal RC branch. This effect is admissible when leakage is not negligible over the sampled time range; if leakage is extremely weak or data stop very early, the refinement becomes hard to identify, which should be stated rather than exaggerated.

derivation_notes: The constant-capacitance assumption is relaxed by replacing capacitance with an effective differential capacitance capacitance * (1 + capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity * tanh(Abs(V_C) / capacitance_voltage_scale)). This keeps the parent charging and leakage currents but divides their effect on dV_C_dt by a voltage-dependent storage factor, so the charging slows more at voltages where the dielectric exhibits increased capacitance.
change_summary: The successor makes capacitance depend on capacitor voltage, introducing a state-dependent RC timescale without adding new states or inputs. This changes the target mapping itself by altering trajectory curvature at higher |V_C|, especially across runs with different source_voltage.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Capacitance is constant over the observed voltage range.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Voltage-dependent capacitance of the capacitor dielectric alters the effective RC timescale during charging.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent when capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity tends to zero, so the effective capacitance reduces to capacitance.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed capacitance, the charging law has a single RC timescale so dV_C_dt decreases with V_C mainly through one affine charging term plus the existing leakage nonlinearity.
response_change.child_relation: Let capacitance depend on capacitor voltage, so the same source_voltage and resistance produce a voltage-dependent effective charging timescale; dV_C_dt is reduced more strongly in the voltage range where capacitance increases, changing the curvature of V_C(t).
response_change.observable_effect: Across experiments varying source_voltage while holding resistance, nominal low-bias capacitance, and leakage parameters fixed, the rise is relatively slower in the higher-V_C portion of the trajectory for larger source_voltage because the effective capacitance grows with voltage; a single fixed-capacitance parent cannot match both low-voltage and higher-voltage trajectory curvature with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Voltage-dependent capacitance of the capacitor dielectric alters the effective RC timescale during charging.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the storage coefficient changes along the trajectory as a nonlinear function of the observed state, so one shared parameter set must explain curvature changes across source_voltage conditions rather than only rescaling the whole response.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The resistor and capacitor are ideal and time-invariant.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The capacitor's effective differential capacitance varies with applied voltage through dielectric nonlinearity.

evolution_contract.after_fragment: (source_voltage - V_C) / (resistance * capacitance * (1 + capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity * tanh(Abs(V_C) / capacitance_voltage_scale))) - leak_conductance * V_C * tanh(Abs(V_C) / leakage_voltage_scale) / (capacitance * (1 + capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity * tanh(Abs(V_C) / capacitance_voltage_scale)))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity -> 0, which makes the multiplicative capacitance factor equal to 1 and recovers the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For runs starting from V_C(0)=0 with different source_voltage but the same resistance, capacitance, and leakage parameters, the child predicts extra late-trajectory flattening when V_C approaches or exceeds capacitance_voltage_scale, because both charging and leakage-induced voltage change are divided by a larger effective capacitance. The parent retains one fixed storage scale and therefore cannot reproduce the stronger high-voltage curvature with the same low-voltage slope across all runs.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters with a single shared set cannot create a state-dependent slowdown that appears only after V_C enters the capacitance-variation range. Changing capacitance or resistance in the parent rescales the timescale nearly globally, while changing leakage parameters mainly alters the leak branch activation; neither reproduces the specific cross-condition contrast of similar early charging but disproportionately slower high-V_C evolution in larger-source runs.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model treats capacitance as constant, omitting the common dielectric effect that a real capacitor's differential capacitance can vary with applied voltage.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The resistor and capacitor are ideal and time-invariant.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Voltage-dependent capacitance of the capacitor dielectric alters the effective RC timescale during charging.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the constant-capacitance assumption rather than add an unrelated new branch. The parent target mapping effectively uses one fixed storage factor capacitance, so for fixed resistance the charging slope at a given V_C is constrained to one shared RC scaling apart from the already modeled leakage activation. Vary source_voltage across runs, hold resistance and leakage parameters fixed, and observe V_C(t) from the same initial condition V_C(0)=0. In the parent, after refitting one global parameter set, trajectories at different source_voltage remain tied to the same capacitance and therefore to the same basic curvature pattern versus normalized progress, aside from leakage. In the child, if capacitance increases with |V_C|, higher-source runs enter a larger-capacitance regime later in the rise and show extra slowdown near the upper part of the trajectory. This is a changed target mapping because dV_C_dt itself at the observed state V_C changes as a function of V_C through the effective capacitance, not merely an auxiliary hidden trajectory. The effect is admissible when the applied voltage range is large enough for capacitance variation to matter; if the capacitor technology is nearly ideal over the sampled range, the refinement may be weak and the parent is recovered.

derivation_notes: The missing process is series parasitic inductance, which requires a new current state because inductive voltage depends on the time rate of change of current and therefore introduces memory beyond a V_C-only law. The new state starts at I_L=0 immediately after connection, which is the physically correct finite-current initial condition for an inductor and creates the intended delayed startup rather than closing the new branch on an invariant zero-effect set.
change_summary: The capacitor charging term is now driven by a dynamic series current state instead of being algebraically slaved to source_voltage - V_C. This adds an early inductive startup phase with delayed voltage rise before the later RC-like behavior re-emerges.

add_term_audit.parent_reduction: As parasitic_inductance -> 0, or once the fast current transient has relaxed so I_L becomes quasi-steady, the added current dynamics collapse toward the parent's instantaneous charging current law
add_term_audit.observable_signature: Compared at fixed component values with sufficiently fast early-time sampling, the child shows near-zero initial dV_C_dt followed by a short current-ramp phase and possible early inflection, while the parent begins immediately at its largest slope and then only decreases

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps capacitor voltage to its derivative through a single monotone RC charging phase with voltage-dependent capacitance and leakage, so the charging rate decreases smoothly from its initial value without an additional transient stage.
response_change.child_relation: Add a parasitic series inductive current state so the target derivative depends on both capacitor voltage and circuit current, creating an initial current-ramp phase before the usual RC-like approach. The mapping from observed V_C to dV_C_dt is no longer single-valued in time because the same V_C can occur with different current histories during startup.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed source_voltage, resistance, and capacitance, the child predicts delayed initial rise of V_C and possible inflection in the early-time trajectory, whereas the parent always starts with its maximal charging slope at t=0 and then relaxes monotonically.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the parasitic inductive timescale is not negligible relative to the RC charging timescale, i.e. during early-time measurements with fast sampling after connection and physically plausible wiring or lead inductance.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as rounded or delayed startup relative to the later charging tail; in holdout with different resistance or capacitance but similar non-negligible inductive timescale, the same startup phase persists and shifts systematically rather than being absorbed into one global RC constant.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing parasitic inductance or after the fast current transient has relaxed so circuit current becomes quasi-instantaneously slaved to source_voltage - V_C.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: Inductance introduces dynamical memory through current inertia; this cannot be represented by a purely algebraic modification of the existing V_C-only right-hand side because the same V_C can correspond to different charging currents during startup.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: series parasitic inductive current buildup coupled to capacitor charging
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Series parasitic inductance stores magnetic energy and limits the rate of change of charging current, introducing an additional fast transient phase before the capacitor follows the slower resistive-capacitive evolution.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added mechanism is structurally harder because it introduces a hidden current state and applies a nonlinear tanh smoothing to the state-dependent inductive drive, so the target derivative depends on a coupled transient trajectory rather than a single algebraic gain on source_voltage - V_C.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Parasitic inductance is negligible, so charging current responds instantaneously to the voltage difference across the resistor-capacitor path.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Charging current has finite inductive buildup governed by a new current state before approaching the slower resistive-capacitive regime.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take parasitic_inductance -> 0 with inductive_current_smoothing_scale large enough that tanh(I_L/inductive_current_smoothing_scale) stays in its linear regime, yielding rapid relaxation of I_L toward (source_voltage - V_C)/resistance.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With fast early-time observation after connection, dV_C_dt starts near zero because I_L(0)=0, then rises over a short inductive timescale before decaying; the parent instead starts immediately at a positive maximum set by source_voltage/(resistance*capacitance) and has no separate startup phase.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the delayed initial slope and the later tail because its target mapping is algebraic in V_C alone: matching the later RC-like portion fixes an initial slope near source_voltage divided by an effective RC scale, while reducing that slope enough to mimic the inductive startup would also slow the entire subsequent trajectory. The child changes the scored mapping itself, since at the same observed V_C during startup different I_L values give different dV_C_dt.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when the parasitic inductive timescale is not negligible relative to the RC charging timescale, i.e. during early-time measurements with fast sampling after connection and physically plausible wiring or lead inductance.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as rounded or delayed startup relative to the later charging tail; in holdout with different resistance or capacitance but similar non-negligible inductive timescale, the same startup phase persists and shifts systematically rather than being absorbed into one global RC constant.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing parasitic inductance or after the fast current transient has relaxed so circuit current becomes quasi-instantaneously slaved to source_voltage - V_C.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: Inductance introduces dynamical memory through current inertia; this cannot be represented by a purely algebraic modification of the existing V_C-only right-hand side because the same V_C can correspond to different charging currents during startup.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model omits parasitic inductance of leads and connections, which can produce a finite current build-up time immediately after the source is connected.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Parasitic inductance is negligible, so charging current responds instantaneously to the voltage difference across the resistor-capacitor path.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Series parasitic inductance stores magnetic energy and limits the rate of change of charging current, introducing an additional fast transient phase before the capacitor follows the slower resistive-capacitive evolution.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to release the neglected parasitic inductance as a new current-like state. The parent target mapping has a single-phase shortcut: for any admissible experiment starting from V_C=0 with fixed source_voltage, resistance, capacitance, and leakage parameters, dV_C_dt is determined solely by V_C and therefore begins at its largest positive value at connection and then decreases as V_C rises. If we vary the observation regime by comparing slower sampling windows, where the parent is adequate, against fast early-time windows after the switch closes while holding component values fixed, a circuit with non-negligible lead inductance shows a different response: the charging current cannot jump instantly, so dV_C_dt starts near zero, rises over a short inductive timescale, and only then transitions toward the RC-controlled decay. This is a genuine change in the scored target mapping, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because the derivative of V_C at the same observed V_C depends on the hidden current state during the startup transient. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the delayed initial slope and the later charging tail across those conditions, since lowering the parent's effective RC rate to match the startup delay would also slow the entire later trajectory, while fitting the later tail forces an unrealistically large initial slope. The effect is scientifically admissible when measurement bandwidth resolves times comparable to the inductive transient and becomes weak when inductance is negligible or observations begin only after current has equilibrated.

derivation_notes: The fixed-environment capacitance law is relaxed by introducing a lumped thermal state driven by charging dissipation and relaxing on its own thermal timescale. The new state starts at T_th = 0 because the experiment begins from ambient equilibrium; this is a non-degenerate baseline since subsequent current flow drives T_th away from zero and feeds back into the V_C dynamics through the capacitance nonlinearity amplitude.
change_summary: The successor adds electrothermal memory: self-heating during higher-current charging shifts the voltage-dependent capacitance law over time. assumption_audit.released_assumption: The voltage-dependent capacitance law is time-invariant and unaffected by self-heating during charging.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Joule heating during startup raises the component temperature, and dielectric response drifts with that thermal state, altering the effective capacitance-voltage nonlinearity.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when T_th remains zero or when thermal_capacitance_nonlinearity_sensitivity = 0; dynamically, this occurs in the zero-heating limit thermal_heating_gain -> 0 or the instantaneous-thermal-relaxation limit thermal_time_constant -> 0 with finite heating.

response_change.child_relation: Release the fixed-capacitance assumption by allowing the capacitor's effective capacitance nonlinearity to relax with self-heating during charging, so dV_C_dt at the same (V_C, I_L) can differ depending on the accumulated thermal state of the component.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare runs with different source_voltage or resistance but the same nominal capacitor parameters. In the parent, whenever two trajectories pass through the same observed state pair (V_C, I_L), the predicted dV_C_dt must coincide. In the child, stronger earlier current raises T_th, so later in the transient the same (V_C, I_L) can map to a different dV_C_dt through the thermally shifted capacitance nonlinearity. evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce both cool and hot late-transient slopes at the same V_C because the parent only lets temperature act through the common capacitance denominator, not through an additional temperature-scaled leakage subtraction. Refitting leak_conductance or capacitance-related parameters globally would force one compromise leakage level rather than the required T_th-dependent increase across conditions.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping dV_C_dt(V_C,I_L,T_th) uses a thermally drifting capacitance but a temperature-invariant leakage branch, so at fixed electrical state the leakage contribution remains proportional to V_C*tanh(Abs(V_C)/leakage_voltage_scale) with only the shared capacitance denominator changing.
response_change.child_relation: Make the leakage branch itself temperature dependent, so dV_C_dt at fixed V_C and I_L depends on the interaction T_th × V_C through a thermally activated leakage conductance. This changes the balance between charging current and self-discharge as heating accumulates.
response_change.observable_effect: Across runs with different source_voltage or resistance that generate different self-heating histories, late-transient charging slows more strongly at the same V_C when T_th is larger, producing a temperature-linked sag in dV_C_dt and possibly a lower approach rate to the source voltage than the parent can match with one shared leakage parameter set.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when self-heating is non-negligible over the charging window, i.e. thermal_heating_gain*resistance*I_L**2 accumulates enough that T_th departs measurably from zero while V_C is large enough for the leakage branch to be active on the scale leakage_voltage_scale.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, lower- and higher-dissipation trajectories already differ in T_th buildup; in holdout, stronger source_voltage or smaller resistance extends that same mechanism, causing a larger late-time leakage-induced reduction in dV_C_dt at comparable V_C that the parent cannot reproduce with one fixed leakage strength.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the thermal sensitivity of leakage to zero, or in regimes where T_th stays near zero throughout the observation window.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model includes self-heating but assumes the dielectric leakage path is thermally invariant, even though leakage in real capacitors commonly increases with temperature.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The leakage conductance is fixed and independent of the capacitor's thermal state.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-activated dielectric leakage: warming of the capacitor raises carrier mobility or defect-assisted conduction, increasing parallel leakage during the same charging transient that generated the heat.
evolution_plan.rationale: A natural next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-environment treatment of leakage rather than adding a wholly new branch. In the parent, varying source_voltage or resistance changes I_L and therefore T_th, but the target mapping only feels that heating through the capacitance denominator; the leakage numerator itself is unchanged at fixed V_C. In the child, the same thermal state also strengthens leakage, so two trajectories that reach similar V_C but with different prior dissipation histories will have different dV_C_dt because hotter capacitors leak more strongly. Hold capacitance, leak shape scale, and initial conditions fixed; vary source_voltage and/or resistance over admissible monotone-charging conditions so that one case produces modest T_th and another larger T_th. Then compare late transient segments where V_C is already on the order of leakage_voltage_scale and T_th has had time to accumulate. The parent with one shared parameter set can alter capacitance drift through its existing thermal factor, but it cannot create an additional temperature-dependent subtraction in the numerator balance between I_L and leakage. Refitting leak_conductance alone cannot match both low-heating and high-heating cases simultaneously because that would require one leakage level for cool trajectories and a larger leakage level for hot trajectories at the same V_C. The effect is scientifically admissible when self-heating is modest but nonzero; if T_th remains near zero or V_C never reaches the leakage activation scale, this refinement becomes weak and the parent is effectively recovered.

states.rhs: I_L / (capacitance * (1 + capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity * (1 + thermal_capacitance_nonlinearity_sensitivity * T_th) * tanh(Abs(V_C) / capacitance_voltage_scale))) - leak_conductance * (1 + thermal_leakage_sensitivity * T_th) * V_C * tanh(Abs(V_C) / leakage_voltage_scale) / (capacitance * (1 + capacitance_voltage_nonlinearity * (1 + thermal_capacitance_nonlinearity_sensitivity * T_th) * tanh(Abs(V_C) / capacitance_voltage_scale)))
(source_voltage - V_C - resistance * I_L * tanh(Abs(I_L) / inductive_current_smoothing_scale)) / parasitic_inductance

scenario_text: A resistor and capacitor are connected to a constant voltage source, and the capacitor voltage is recorded after the connection is made. The capacitor voltage evolves through charge accumulation while the resistor limits the charging rate. The baseline model neglects leakage, parasitic inductance, and changes in component values with temperature.
